notes.levels: Clearly different from L1: lychgate roof over the entrance, lanterns on all four piers, saplings in every row, sawhorse and cauldron in the yard.

visual.summary: L1 plus a covered lychgate with hanging lanterns, lanterns on the corner piers, oak/birch/spruce saplings in every row, a sawhorse, cauldron, barrel and shutters on the shed window.
problems: Leaves of the two young oaks run into the shed eave: leaf at (8,5,6) sits on the roof stair and leaves at (2,3,6)/(8,3,6) press against the shed posts, so from the front the canopies swallow the shed; trim them back so the eave at z=6 is clear.

Shed interior is a 3 x 1 alcove (x4..6, z8) holding chest, grindstone and barrel in a row: reads as a stall more than a woodcutter's shed; give it a real working depth (2 deep) or turn it into an open-fronted lean-to with a bench.

Reach: the shed floor, workstation (chest, grindstone, barrel), yard and every planting row are reached; the unreached places are roof slopes, leaf tops, pier tops and the gateway roof, which is fine.

Carlton's v1 note (all levels) is not met: sapling spots must stay clear, and decoration belongs outside the planting area. L2 adds a barrel at (4,0,4) and a cauldron at (6,0,5) inside the plot beside the path. Move them by the shed or the log yard.
